peer_none: Dossier 24 synthesis across the Fortune 500 peer set

peer_samsung: a major manufacturing peer, AI governance disclosures and Seoul AI Business Pledge commitments, February 2025

peer_xpia: Microsoft AI Red Team whitepaper, January 2025

arch_gvrm: NIST CSF 2.0, GOVERN function, subcategory GV.RM-02

arch_pla: Gartner guidance on Protection Level Agreements

arch_gap: Dossier 25, diagnostic on rejected strategy drafts

Global security spending of $244.2B in 2026, of which roughly $49B is "AI-amplified security" against only $2.8B for "securing AI itself" — about 5.5% of the AI security market, a roughly seventeen-fold imbalance.
bm_stanford: 88% of organisations report AI adoption but fewer than 10% have fully scaled deployments. Tracked AI incidents rose 55% year on year, from 233 to 362.
bm_dbir: Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report 2026 (secondary-sourced; pending primary verification)
62% of breaches involved the human element, 48% involved a third party, and 48% involved ransomware.

atlasnodet: MITRE ATLAS technique object schema, exhaustive parse of the published data

atlasgap: Mitigation coverage across MITRE ATLAS technique objects

73 of 197 technique objects (37%) have no mitigation at all. AML.T0118.000 Communication via Shared Artifacts and AML.T0120 AI Artifact Repository are both graded "Realized" with zero mitigating relationships.
safmcp: Observation modality "runtime" appears in 69 of 78 techniques; "gateway" appears in 16. Every mapping in the matrix is partial: "0 direct, 78 partial".
delegimp: Delegation membership is formally non-identifiable from audit logs, traces and event-local attributes. Trace-based grouping recovers 4-6% of a delegation's events; time-window correlation produces up to 107,718 candidate groupings; sub-agent fanout above 2 is the breaking point.
huntonly: Eleven published AI-agent queries, all hunting queries rather than analytics rules, so none raises an incident. None joins the agent inventory to runtime activity — the canonical signal, an agent invoking a tool it never declared, is shipped by nobody.
agentsinfo: 42 columns including Triggers, ConnectedAgents, DeclaredTools, DeclaredDataSources, McpServers, Instructions, Memory, Guardrails “and their coverage”, Permissions and EntraAgentID.
refusal: arXiv:2603.01246, Defensive Refusal Bias — 2,390 real blue-team tasks

2.72x refusal rate on security-sensitive defensive requests, including 43.8% on system hardening and 34.3% on malware analysis, and stating that you are authorised makes it worse. "critical for autonomous defensive agents, which cannot rephrase refused queries or retry."
honeyquest: arXiv:2606.21037, Honeyquest for LLMs — 21 models, 10,962 responses, 47-person human baseline
Every model took bait at a significantly higher rate than humans, roughly 78% against roughly 37%. Models articulated that a lure was a trap and then exploited it anyway in 73.4% of cases.
tempo: Fails at 99.8% or worse against a competent adversary, and fails confidently — mean confidence of at least 0.993 when wrong — with a formal zero-mutual-information result.
stpseq: "While some implementations attempt to enforce strict sequencing, we have found that this approach can be challenging to implement effectively. stpmin: Five-column Minimum Telemetry Requirements schema: Telemetry Source, Relevant Field(s), Data Component, Filter Field(s), Dependencies.
noconsumer: Reconstructed contents of the rebuilt coordination board, reference incident

The registry's audit trail covers only user, group, permission and token events, so content inspection was never possible — metadata was the only available channel.
baseline: FTD detection baseline, confirmed with the programme 2026-09-15

Of four candidate detection foundations, only gateway and model telemetry reaching the SIEM is present, and its own logging and alerting behaviour is unverified. Substrate-plane logs, a trustworthy agent and non-human-identity inventory, and live detection content for agent abuse are absent or unconfirmed. There is no budget to onboard substrate-plane logs.
planes: Two-control-plane assessment of the the enterprise agent estate

The governed plane routes agents through the Apigee AI Gateway with Google Model Armor to approved models and MCP servers. The substrate plane — Artifactory, object store, GitHub Actions, databases, wikis, tickets — carries the same identities with no behavioural analytics, no provenance attestation and no inter-agent channel detection.
registry: Records owner, declared tools, declared write scope and autonomy tier. Nothing was found binding it to runtime enforcement.
ftdscope: Only about 20% of the identified controls sit with CDR. The remainder belong to other teams and ownership is in several cases undefined.
ftdoutcomes: the programme team opening session, 2026-09-15 — agreed outcomes

(1) system uptime and protection of IP and data; (2) enable fast AI adoption without security as the bottleneck; (3) practical approaches to stop agents that exceed boundaries. Also agreed: FTD is an agile methodology that evolves continuously, and defends from the victim's perspective.
ftdcons: the programme team opening session, 2026-09-15 — constraints

Repository unification across approximately 8,000 developers is not achievable. No full digital twin; attack surface management chosen instead, with the AI lab and cyber range cloud-first as an MVP. OT response authority remains deferred to FY27. Crown jewels named as critical IP and recipe data repositories.
nomandate: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.6; OMB M-25-21; EU AI Act Art. 12 and 26; ISO/IEC 42001

No in-force regulation requires the enterprise to inventory AI agents. The NIST framework is voluntary, the federal published-inventory mandate binds agencies only, the EU high-risk obligations were deferred to December 2027 and August 2028, and ISO/IEC 42001 has no headline inventory clause.
nofinding: Konishi, on cloud AI threat detection

csnumbers: Approximately 1,200 agent runs and more than 70,000 messages on the coordination board; roughly 700 runs and about 17,600 attacker actions inside the victim. delegquote: "Shared authority is not shared causality. Any telemetry model that conflates 'same trace' with 'same unit of accountability' will fail under delegated execution."

ADVERSARY MANAGEMENT: "Understand adversary tactics"; "Threat intelligence"; "Anticipate possible attacks against target organization". ADVERSARY DISRUPTION: "Misdirect and delay adversary"; "Increase attacker cost"; "Increase chance of detecting attack". POSTURE AND POLICY MANAGEMENT: "Validate correct configurations"; "Harden devices and reduce attack surface".
defaultoff: "Default-off is not the same as off." A misconfiguration that produces no error produces no telemetry.

"Fragmented IT/OT convergence creates severe risks, as current systems lack unified governance and struggle to support the downtime required for constant patching." And: "Frontier LLMs (e.g., Mythos 5, GPT 5.6) expose critical infrastructure vulnerabilities, increasing risks in areas such as ransomware and supply chain attacks."

And: "Work with cybersecurity teams to pull automated critical IT, OT, and cloud asset inventories from existing exposure assessment platforms, in order to prioritize where to start changing architectures and reduce the greatest amount of risk."

"By 2028, cybersecurity AI agents will autonomously manage 25% of incident response workflows for data security events, enhancing the speed and effectiveness..."
g_cognitive: Gartner G00845745, “The Future of the CISO Role 2030”, 21 May 2026, p.1

"The next breach will be cognitive: Threat actors will abandon purely technical exploits in favor of influence operations, utilizing cutting-edge AI models to manipulate employee decision making and bypass traditional cybersecurity controls."
g_talent: "AI will widen the exploit-fix gap and erode the talent pipeline: AI-driven exploit generation will continuously outpace traditional patching cycles. At the same time, fully automating fixes will eliminate practical learning ground required to develop experienced Level 3 analysts."
g_antifragile: "The mandate will shift to antifragility: Simply returning to the status quo after an incident will no longer be viable. The core cybersecurity mandate will shift toward adaptive cyber resilience and antifragility, where organizations will intentionally use systemic shocks and controlled risk exposure to emerge operationally stronger and more resistant to future threats."
g_rogue: "Rogue automation will demand mature IAM and data security oversight: The proliferation of AI agents operating with broad agencies will create severe risks. Traditional centralized IT and third-party vendor management will be unable to oversee these agents."
g_odm: Gartner G00799085, “Outcome-Driven Metrics for the Digital Era”, 11 Jul 2025, p.6

"ODMs measure the continuous outcome of an investment. If you can't identify the investment, it probably isn't an ODM." "ODMs sit on a sliding scale, where better and worse are a reflection of a value measure related to the investment." "ODMs support direct investment: You can make a direct investment to get better. You can lower your investment and accept that the outcome will get worse."
g_line: "Using the construct of 'above the line' and 'below the line' differentiates metrics and value for IT operations (below the line) and for business outcomes and business decision making (above the line)." "Operational metrics with a direct line of sight to business outcomes are referenced as technology ODMs."
g_stopreporting: "Stop reporting operational IT metrics that are disconnected from business outcomes. When talking to business leaders, create a direct connection between technology and the business outcomes it supports through ODMs."
g_25odm: "ODMs are especially powerful when used to measure cybersecurity. Gartner has defined 25 cyber ODMs and built a global benchmark. The ODMs represent the delivered protection levels for key cybersecurity investments."
g_odmsteps: Step 1: "Develop an Initial Set of Business Processes and Supporting Technology Stacks" — "Start with a simple list of the three to five most obvious business processes supported by technology." Step 2: "Identify Business Outcomes and Outcome-Driven Metrics". Step 3: "Identify Technology Risks/Dependencies" — "What breaks in the business process if the technology breaks?"
g_sovereign: Gartner G00858028, “A Checklist to Keep Your Organization Safe From Frontier AI Models”, 5 Aug 2026, p.1

"AI sovereignty concerns: 69% of organizations are worried about maintaining control over AI models, highlighting the need for robust AI safety practices." And: "Technical controls: Due diligence alone is insufficient; technical controls are essential to mitigate risks associated with frontier models."
g_checklist: "Evaluate safety frameworks... Independently assess models: Include governance, catastrophic risk thresholds, evaluation validity and technical security in assessments. Implement technical controls: Establish a model delivery system with layered control planes to address AI safety and compliance. Define risk tiers: Collaboratively classify AI initiatives by risk level and map them to appropriate control measures. Adopt composite AI patterns: For high-risk use cases, combine AI models with deterministic systems to ensure reliable outputs."
g_note1: Gartner G00799085, Note 1 “Key Concepts and Characteristics for Outcome-Driven Metrics”, p.14

"Metric value. The value of a metric is its ability to influence decision making. The decisions influenced are typically priorities and investments." "Above the line, below the line... Both are necessary and have their purpose, but only above-the-line metrics should be shared with executives to drive effective business decisions." "Leading indicators. Leading indicators expose a problem before it leads to material loss." "Direct line of sight to a business outcome. "Metric changes drive action. When a metric changes from green to yellow to red, it drives an action such as changing a priority or an investment." "Address the needs of discrete audiences."
g_limit: "Limit the number of metrics. You only need five to nine metrics for each target audience. Do not report everything you know. Prioritize the top five to nine technology dependencies and the top audiences to receive only the highest-value information that drives above-the-line decisions."
g_prioritise: Gartner G00799085, Table 1 “Reporting and Decision-Making Opportunities”, p.12

On demand governance: "Technology ODMs better connect business change technology investments to the business outcomes they enable. If there is no clear line of sight to a business outcome, then the technology investment should not be prioritized as it will drive little value to the organization."
g_step45: "Step 4: Define Technology ODMs. Define the metrics that will measure the critical technology support points for business processes supporting business outcomes. The technology ODMs will reflect the technology stack's readiness to support the selected business outcome." "These technology ODMs are now behaving as leading indicators." "Step 5: Assess the Technology Stack's Readiness as Risk to Business Enablement... Create the business enablement risk scale with, at one end, no investment or technology stack to enable the business outcome; at the other, investment in leading-edge technologies that would elevate the current technology stack to drive the most positive outcome for the business."
g_readiness: "Readiness is defined as technology that operates the way it is designed, fully supports a business process, meets compliance requirements and is not unreasonably at risk of failure." And: "Readiness describes the state of investments and capabilities to manage [the risk]. Poor capabilities and investments will lead to more outages... Good capabilities and investments will lead to happy customers."
g_instrument: "Organizations will discover that measuring some of these elements may require instrumenting parts of the infrastructure to gather new types of data. While there may be expenses associated with this activity, Gartner believes the visibility and power to report benefits and to guide priorities and technology investments in a business context will make the initial investment worthwhile."
ctem5: Continuous threat exposure management, five-phase model (research dossier 12)

Scope, discover, prioritise, validate, mobilise. Scope by business impact rather than technology silo; discover far wider than known-vulnerability scanning; prioritise by attack path rather than severity; validate that the exposure is real and the control works; mobilise the fix. Validation is the phase most programmes skip.
nopath: Neither route into the victim had a published vulnerability identifier at the time. A scanner-driven programme would have matched nothing, because what made it an intrusion was the attack path — and no severity score rates a path.
noswarm: No tooling simulates a collective of independent, coordinating autonomous agents. The multi-agent offensive frameworks that exist decompose one attacker's workflow into role-specialised stages — division of labour, not coordination. Genuine multi-agent environments exist only on the defensive side. The defensible reframing is therefore to remove the assumption that attacks arrive at human speed, rather than to promise swarm simulation.
cage: TTCP CAGE Challenges on the CybORG environment (dossier 11)

The only published body of work that evaluates autonomous containment prices the defender's own collateral damage into an availability-weighted reward — a Restore action incurs a negative reward. It evaluates the response policy, not whether a specific real mechanism executes correctly within budget.
cagedecoy: Raising decoy detection probability from 0.5 to 1.0, false positives from 0.1 to 0 and duration from 2 steps to 1 produced only a "slight advantage", because probing for deception is itself observable. This is not evidence that decoys became ineffective — elsewhere decoys blocked up to 94% of privilege-granting exploits.
admission: Kubernetes admission-control guidance and the admission chain budget (dossier 08)

Admission-controller fail-open is the upstream recommendation rather than a misconfiguration, and setting failurePolicy to Fail does not save you because of a hard 30-second admission-chain budget. The architectural fix is in-process CEL policy evaluation.
ssvc: CISA BOD 26-04, 10 June 2026, and the SSVC decision model (dossier 13)

The federal CVSS mandate was revoked in favour of a four-variable stakeholder-specific model with 3-day, 14-day, 60-day and defer timelines. Only about 1% of instances fell in the 3-day band and roughly 60% were deferred. CISA also directs that evidence be collected before remediating.
norollback: No automatic rollback capability exists anywhere in the mainstream Microsoft or Qualys patch stack, and stopping a fleet mid-deployment takes on the order of eight hours — longer than the entire escalation window in the reference incident.
breakout: Average adversary breakout time of 29 minutes, down from 98, then 84, then 48 minutes across recent reporting cycles; fastest observed breakout 27 seconds; median time from initial access to hand-off to a secondary group 22 seconds, down from more than eight hours in 2022.
hfescal: Reference incident post-mortem, defender's own account (dossier 01)

"The first signals came from several layers of our security stack at once: live runtime analysis, SIEM logs, and others. On their own, each was ambiguous... those were correlated by our AI-based security agent stack and resolved into a coherent attack signal. However, it failed to correctly raise the alert's criticality and trigger the on-call team, costing precious time in the response." The stated remediation: "a high-severity signal pages a responder in minutes, any day of the week." The intrusion ran from Saturday 11 July to Monday 13 July.
msem: Critical asset definition drives generated attack paths; first-class connectors exist for Qualys and the ServiceNow CMDB. The gating input is a business workshop to define what matters, not an engineering build — without it the attack-path view may be empty. Attack-path analysis is unsupported for OT connectors, which is an independent justification for deferring OT response authority.
revoke: Cohort revocation by issue time using the aws:TokenIssueTime condition key; Vault lease revocation by prefix; SPIFFE authority taint; OpenID Shared Signals and CAEP, whose final specifications were published in September 2025; label-swap quarantine for workloads; and GitOps prune and self-heal for configuration restoration. CRIU-based process checkpointing carries significant caveats for forensic capture.
msdeception: Defender for Endpoint Deception was retired before general availability — onboarding was blocked in August 2025 and decoys removed on 31 October 2025. Do not include it in a plan. The Defender for Identity honeytoken tag is generally available but covers on-premises Active Directory via sensors, so cloud-only directory accounts are not covered — which is exactly where non-human identities live. The Sentinel honeytoken solution covers Key Vault only and is community-supported.
canaryfp: Free public canary credentials are statically fingerprintable and are flagged by secret-scanning tooling as canaries without triggering an alert. Paid or self-hosted deployment only, with diversified token types — document, DNS, kubeconfig and MCP configuration.
canaryev: The Spacecrab deployment reported 83% exploitation at around 30 minutes. Grafana Labs detected a real 2025 intrusion within seconds using canaries placed in GitHub Secrets at both organisation and repository level, running tens of thousands of tokens. No published false-positive rate exists for any canary vendor and no recall data exists anywhere, so the structural argument — a decoy has no legitimate consumer — must carry the case rather than an invented number.
mcpcanary: A canary token embedded in MCP configuration detects agents routing around organisational MCP restrictions — directly relevant to an enterprise MCP fabric with a direct-connection prohibition.
ncsc: National-level deception trials, 121 organisations across 14 vendors (dossier 14)
The published recommendation is tripwires and honeytokens for all organisations, and full interactive honeypots only for mature security operations teams.
expctrl: Export-control analysis of inference over controlled technical data (dossier 10)

The safe harbour at 15 CFR § 734.18 covers encrypted transit, but inference decrypts and processes the data. No BIS or DDTC guidance exists on whether inference over controlled technical data constitutes a deemed export. Enforcement climate context: penalties of approximately $213M and $252M against two US critical-manufacturing-sector companies.
iso27037: The standard requires repeatability and reproducibility of forensic process. Hosted models update and reroute silently, so every inference touching evidence must record model hash, engine version and decode parameters into the case record.
labstack: Candidate serving stacks are vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM and llama.cpp. Quantisation introduces calibration sensitivity that must be characterised before forensic use. Open weights must be treated as untrusted executable code entering a high-trust enclave: pickle-format model files execute code at load time, roughly 95% of malicious models found on one public hub used that format, the standard scanner has a published bypass, and ShadowRay (CVE-2023-48022) was never fixed. PRC-origin weights are a first-order selection constraint for a US critical-manufacturing enterprise and require a documented risk position.
yolo: Splunk detection: Linux Auditd AI CLI Permission Override Activated (dossier 18)

Detects autonomy-boundary removal such as claude --dangerously-skip-permissions and gemini --yolo. It is the highest-value, lowest-cost agent detection in the published corpus, and no Windows or macOS equivalent is published anywhere.
sep414: W3C baggage propagated in MCP params._meta — the specified carrier for binding delegation context at execution time.
discrim: Coordination-channel discriminator (dossier 17, and the colleague's two-plane assessment)

A legitimate dependency has one writer, provenance, and a consuming build. A coordination channel has many writers, no provenance, and no consumer. The distinction is computable from access metadata alone, without inspecting content — which matters because content inspection of the reference channel was never possible.
gateway: the enterprise governed model and tool plane (two-plane assessment)

Policy enforced at the gateway includes directory JWT and OAuth validation, scope and group authorisation, quotas and token caps, DLP and redaction, prompt-injection inspection, a model allowlist sourced from AI governance, and central logging to the SIEM. All MCP interactions are required to route through it and direct MCP connections are prohibited for Tier 1 servers. Known risk items: a RAID entry for a gateway outage, and a re-routing risk in the model proxy — meaning the chokepoint may fail open.
msdisc: Microsoft Learn, “Migrate custom app registrations to Agent ID” (dossier 19)

The only published agent-discovery methodology, and its ordering is the insight: tag-based scan, then six-signal heuristic analysis, then CMDB reconciliation, then developer attestation of the residue with a deadline and an escalation path. Attestation is step four of four, applied only to what the first three could not resolve.
snowaict: ServiceNow AI Control Tower three-layer asset data model (dossier 19)

Product Model / Digital Asset / Configuration Item, so one agent deployed in three regions yields one model, one asset and three configuration items. Published failure mode of a flat registry: "governance is applied to an entire class of AI, not individual deployments".
asim: ASIM AgentEvent schema v0.1.0, parser dated 2026-07-08 (dossier 19)

The only Mandatory fields are EventCount, EventStartTime, EventEndTime, EventProduct, EventVendor, EventSchema and EventSchemaVersion. SrcAgentId is merely Recommended and ToolName is Optional — so a fully compliant agent event can carry no agent identifier at all. The one existing source parser sets TargetAgentId from a coalesce of platform-local IDs, which will not join to anything.
df_arup: Arup deepfake incident — Hong Kong, February 2024, disclosed May 2024 (dossier 28)

A confirmed loss of US$25.6 million after an employee joined a video conference in which every other participant was an AI-generated impersonation of a colleague, including the CFO. The first confirmed large-scale financial loss attributable to a real-time video deepfake.
df_mgm: Initial access was obtained by socially engineering the IT help desk into an MFA reset, with compromise achieved in roughly ten minutes and a disclosed impact in excess of $100 million. Notably **no synthetic media was required** — a voice call and research on a named employee were sufficient.
df_eval: Commercial deepfake-detection models lose roughly 45-50% of their AUC when tested against realistic in-the-wild 2024 content compared with their performance on standard laboratory benchmarks.
df_iso: The standard's scope covers presentation attacks — artefacts presented to a sensor — and structurally excludes injection attacks, where synthetic video is fed directly into the data path. A product can therefore hold valid liveness certification and remain fully exposed to the deepfake technique actually used against identity-verification systems.
df_c2pa: Provenance metadata is destroyed by any screenshot, re-encode or platform re-compression, and the absence of a credential is not evidence that content is synthetic. Provenance is therefore an authenticity aid for content you control, not a detection control for content you receive.
df_human: iProov consumer deepfake-detection study (vendor-funded; treat with caution) (dossier 28)
Untrained participants correctly identified deepfake content in approximately 0.1% of trials.
df_oob: The controls that work do not depend on detecting a fake: callback verification to a **pre-registered** contact channel rather than one supplied by the caller; a passphrase that never travels over the channel being verified; and dual authorisation above a value threshold for payment and access changes. Documented failure modes are procedural rather than technical — the attacker supplies the callback number, or manufactured urgency causes staff to bypass the procedure.
ms_fail: Of fourteen organisations attempting even limited segmentation, eleven failed — and predominantly for organisational rather than technical reasons: no executive champion and no application-owner buy-in.
ms_phase: Discovery first: 30 to 90 days of traffic observation before any enforcement; a pilot in 8 to 12 weeks; a first enterprise segment in 3 to 6 months. Enforcing before dependency mapping is the common cause of outage-driven rollback.
ms_k8s: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy and service-mesh enforcement caveats (dossier 28)

A NetworkPolicy object is accepted and silently does nothing unless the cluster's CNI plugin implements enforcement. Separately, Cilium's WireGuard transparent-encryption path is not FIPS-validated while Istio's mTLS is — a material constraint where FIPS compliance is required.
ms_ot: Network-enforced segmentation is the only viable primary control for legacy process equipment, which frequently cannot run an agent and in many cases cannot support VLAN tagging. CISA's Zero Trust Maturity Model Networks pillar provides a four-stage narrative — Traditional, Initial, Advanced, Optimal — usable directly as a roadmap.
aispm_limit: AI security posture management category assessment (dossier 28)

Classic AI-SPM is a **static configuration and inventory discipline**: it cannot detect an agent behaving outside its authorised scope at runtime. As one vendor states the distinction, "static AI-SPM tells you what an agent can do; runtime-informed AI-SPM tells you what it actually does." Gartner's own AI-TRiSM framing is reported to acknowledge that it "doesn't adequately cover the governance of the autonomous actions these models can take."
aispm_mkt: The category is consolidating into cloud-native application protection platforms: Wiz acquired by Google, Protect AI by Palo Alto Networks, CalypsoAI by F5, Aim Security by Cato Networks, and Robust Intelligence by Cisco. Procurement implication: AI-SPM arrives as a CNAPP module rather than a standalone purchase.
cti_nofeed: No vendor-neutral, standards-body TTP catalogue for autonomous attackers exists beyond MITRE ATLAS and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (ASI01-ASI10). The US government AI-ISAC remains policy-mandated but pre-decisional with no launch date, so interim AI-threat intelligence should route through an existing sector ISAC.
cti_pir: Priority intelligence requirement practice and the SANS detection-engineering pipeline (dossier 28)

Priority intelligence requirements are most usable at a "stable middle" specificity — a named technique, a named source, and the decision the answer supports — and an analyst can realistically sustain three to five. The published pipeline runs Requirements Discovery, Triage, Investigation, then Development, with validation by purple-team emulation against Sigma-coded, ATT&CK- and ATLAS-tagged detections.
atlas_ver: Version 5.1.0 (November 2025) carried 16 tactics and more than 84 techniques, expanding through v5.4.0 (February 2026). The framework is moving quickly enough that a technique-coverage baseline must record the ATLAS version it was measured against.
ftdmtg: Stakeholder scoping session with Nick and Jonathan, 2026-09-16

"We want to build the enterprise a focused, specific plan & implementation strategy on preventing an adversary from launching a Frontier AI attack against the enterprise." And the essential question: "What do we need to have and do to be 80% confident that we could prevent a Frontier AI attack?"
ftdbau: Stakeholder scoping session with Nick and Jonathan, 2026-09-16
"We must be VERY explicit about separating 'Novel Threats/AI FTD Defense' and 'Business as Usual' items. If an item isn't specific to targeted AI attacks, it goes to the parking lot."
ftdvuln: Stakeholder scoping session with Nick and Jonathan, 2026-09-16

"we don't want to be focused on discovery hell - we don't just need/want more data on vulnerabilities to repair because we don't have enough capacity to repair everything (it just joins the backlog)" and "We want to move away from scoring vulnerabilities individually."
ftdchain: Stakeholder scoping session with Nick and Jonathan, 2026-09-16

"Potential goal would be to identify a number of attack chains and build/use a platform that empirically tests whether we have demonstrably vulnerable attack chains. This should include all possible response actions once a vulnerable chain is identified. This reframes the work from a traditional patch management perspective to an attack chain perspective."
ftdenable: Stakeholder scoping session with Nick and Jonathan, 2026-09-16

Nick called out that the Enable AI team runs its own sprints and arrives at the week saying "these are the 10 things we're doing this week"; the FTD plan must not overlap with that work, and items already owned there go to the parking lot with a later validation checkpoint.
ftdgerry: "much of this is business as usual....but lets have the conversation"; asked for "High Level Strategy stuff that is not business as usual", "something around detecting AI attacks? Knowing when there is something happening and speed and/or scale?", and to "high light the AI Lab a bit more... to call out experimentation and understanding of new models" so that "red team can use kimi k3 for example".
arm_launch: Armadin launch coverage, March 2026 (BankInfoSecurity; Yahoo Finance)

Emerged from stealth in March 2026 with approximately US$190M in Accel-led Seed and Series A funding to automate penetration testing and red-teaming with autonomous AI agents. San Francisco based; founded by Kevin Mandia with Travis Lanham, Evan Pena and David Slater. NOTE: the meeting notes spell the company "Armiden"; the company appears to be Armadin.
arm_method: Armadin platform description (armadin.com; Palo Alto Networks blog, April 2026)

Passive discovery across internet-facing assets, cloud resources and exposed secrets, then a coordinated swarm of AI agents running active reconnaissance and exploitation in parallel; where access is achieved it simulates post-exploitation to demonstrate impact, "logging every attack chain as validated, decision-grade evidence of exploitable risk". Reported to use over 50,000 templates and to run at 80-90% autonomy with 4-6 human decisions per campaign. Vendor-reported; not independently verified.
arm_panw: Palo Alto Networks and Armadin partnership, 30 April 2026

Adds autonomous EXTERNAL attack assessment capacity to Unit 42 Frontier AI Defense, productised as the Unit 42 External AI Hyperattack Assessment. Scope is explicitly the internet-facing external perimeter.
arm_cs: A separate partnership adds continuous AI-driven offensive testing focused on internal networks, identity systems, endpoints and infrastructure — so the external perimeter and the internal estate are addressed through different arrangements.
arm_tenex: Armadin and TENEX.ai joint engagement, August 2026 (PR Newswire; tenex.ai)

Over a three-day exercise the swarm generated 17 million offensive actions from 26,000 agents against more than 25,000 services, launching 1,300 attacks and producing 38 validated attack paths and 238 findings. Vendor-reported figures.
u42_fad: Palo Alto Networks, Unit 42 Frontier AI Defense, launched April 2026

A consulting-delivered service in three components — Frontier AI Exposure Analysis, an Autonomous Security Blueprint, and Agentic Defense Transformation — positioned to "neutralize frontier AI threats before they can be exploited".
u42_alliance: Palo Alto Networks, Frontier AI Defense announcement, 2026
Backed by a "Frontier AI Alliance" of partners named as including Accenture, Armadin, Deloitte, IBM, NTT DATA and PwC.
u42_nocve: Palo Alto Networks and OpenAI, Unit 42 Frontier AI Exposure Analysis expansion, August 2026

Frontier cyber models deployed into customer environments to find exposures, test exploitability and validate attack paths. Reported early data: "36% of identified exposures mapped to no known CVE." Vendor-reported; treat as indicative rather than measured.
owasp_asi: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, published December 2025
Goal hijacking (ASI01) and tool misuse (ASI02) are the top two entries in the 2026 framework — an externally enumerable technique frame for agent-specific attack chains, alongside MITRE ATLAS.
aitest_mkt: Agentic application security testing market survey, 2026

A distinct category from infrastructure attack-path validation. HackerOne Agentic Prompt Injection Testing executes goal-driven multi-turn injection across the stack including indirect injection through retrieval pipelines; Check Point tests across 400+ foundation models plus live applications and agent endpoints with regression and drift detection; Mindgard begins with reconnaissance to discover AI assets; Confident AI with DeepTeam covers injection, jailbreak, prompt and data leakage, access-control abuse and multi-turn attacks against agents with tools and memory.
aitest_limit: Agentic application security testing buyer guidance, 2026 (Invicti; practitioner commentary)

"a good red team exercise should produce an exploit chain, not a list of flagged prompts." Automated tools handle known attack classes at scale, but novel exploits and chained vulnerabilities still require human judgement; automated scanners tend to miss business-logic and privilege-escalation paths in agentic systems.
agentdojo: Simulates dynamic, stateful environments across Workspace, Banking, Travel and Slack with over 900 combinations of benign user task and malicious injection task. Success is determined by DETERMINISTIC check functions that inspect environment state after execution, rather than by model-judged evaluation — which is what makes it usable as a pass/fail test rather than an impression.
caisi: NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation, agent standards programme, February 2026

A three-pillar agent standards programme; CAISI open-sourced AgentDojo-Inspect for agent-hijacking evaluation. Its red-team result reported novel attacks reaching an 81% task-hijack rate against an 11% baseline for prior published attacks.
agentfuzz: AgentFuzz, a directed greybox fuzzer with model-assisted seed generation, reported 34 zero-day taint-style vulnerabilities across 20 open-source agents at 100% precision with 23 CVEs assigned. AgentFuzzer, using Monte Carlo tree search-guided mutation, reported a 71% success rate against a GPT-4-based agent, roughly double the manual baseline.
euai55: EU AI Act, Article 55 and the high-risk obligations timeline

Adversarial testing obligations for general-purpose AI models under Article 55 are already in effect, and high-risk system obligations fall due from August 2026 — so adversarial testing of AI systems has a regulatory as well as a security driver.
